key_insight: The nonlinear entropy-stable extension of Navier–Stokes–Fourier becomes a fourth-order quasi-cubic system in entropy variables, while its quasi-linear approximation preserves the highest-order derivatives and entropy stability.
engineering_relevance: The closure offers a continuum-model route to improved rarefied-gas heat-transfer predictions between parallel plates.
method: Reformulate the nonlinear closure using entropy variables and an inverse-collision-operator derivative identity.
Apply an entropy-stable quasi-linear approximation to stationary parallel-plate heat transfer.
Analyze plane-wave dispersion in the one-dimensional linearized equations.
evidence_signal: With boundary conditions interpolating between continuum and collisionless limits, temperature profiles agree better with DSMC and heat flux agrees better with Sherman–Lees than Navier–Stokes–Fourier predictions; all modes in the linearized dispersion study are stable.
watch_item: Reported heat-transfer gains depend on the boundary-condition specification, and the abstract does not establish performance for multidimensional or turbulent flows.
paper_title: Extensions to the Navier-Stokes-Fourier Equations for Rarefied Transport: Entropy Variable Formulation, Heat Transfer and Dispersion of a Non-Linear Entropy Stable Closure
